sentences.nl: Vandaag oefenen we zinnen, met de grammatica van #dutchgrammar-2, les 10 en 11, over de bijzin, en voegwoorden van tijd en voorwaarde.
sentences.en: Today we are practicing sentences with the grammar of #dutchgrammar-2, lessons 10 and 11, about the subordinate clause, and conjunctions of time and condition.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Today practice we sentences, with the grammar of #dutchgrammar-2, lesson 10 and 11, about the subordinate clause, and conjunctions of time and condition.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Vandaag oefenen we zinnen" follows the Dutch word order of time-manner-place, where "vandaag" (today) sets the time.  
• "Met de grammatica van" uses "met" (with) to indicate the topic or tool being used.  
• "Over de bijzin, en voegwoorden van tijd en voorwaarde" lists topics using "en" (and) to connect them.  
• Example: "Morgen leren we werken met de computer." (Tomorrow we learn to work with the computer.)  
• Example: "Hij praat over de geschiedenis en cultuur van Nederland." (He talks about the history and culture of the Netherlands.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Vandaag bespreken we de regels, met het boek van #dutchgrammar-1, hoofdstuk 5 en 6, over werkwoorden en hun tijden." (Today we discuss the rules, with the book of #dutchgrammar-1, chapters 5 and 6, about verbs and their tenses.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Dutch language courses often use structured grammar resources like "#dutchgrammar" to systematically teach elements like subordinate clauses and conjunctions, which are crucial for mastering Dutch sentence construction.

sentences.nl: De volgende voegwoorden gaan we oefenen:, voordat, nadat, zodra, terwijl, als en wanneer.
sentences.en: The following conjunctions we will practice: before, after, as soon as, while, if, and when.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The following conjunctions are we going to practice: before, after, as soon as, while, if and when.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "De volgende voegwoorden" means "the following conjunctions." "De" is the definite article, and "volgende" is an adjective meaning "following" or "next."  
• The structure "gaan we oefenen" translates to "are we going to practice." Here, "gaan" (to go) is used to indicate a future intention or plan, followed by "oefenen" (to practice).  
• Conjunctions like "voordat" (before), "nadat" (after), "zodra" (as soon as), "terwijl" (while), "als" (if), and "wanneer" (when) are used to connect clauses and indicate the relationship in time or condition.

Examples:  
- "De volgende keer gaan we zwemmen." (Next time we are going to swim.)  
- "Voordat ik naar bed ga, lees ik een boek." (Before I go to bed, I read a book.)  
- "Terwijl hij kookt, luistert hij naar muziek." (While he cooks, he listens to music.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• De volgende plaatsen gaan we bezoeken: Amsterdam, Rotterdam en Utrecht. (The following places we are going to visit: Amsterdam, Rotterdam, and Utrecht.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Conjunctions like "als" and "wanneer" are commonly used in both formal and informal Dutch, but "als" is often used in casual contexts while "wanneer" might be preferred in more formal writing.

sentences.nl: De studenten staan buiten bij hun fiets,, nadat ze 2 uur les hebben gehad.
sentences.en: The students are outside by their bikes after having had 2 hours of class.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• The students stand outside by their bicycle, after they 2 hours lesson have had.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "De studenten staan buiten bij hun fiets" uses the present tense verb "staan" to describe the current action of standing.  
• "nadat ze 2 uur les hebben gehad" is a subordinate clause introduced by "nadat" (after), which causes inversion in Dutch. The auxiliary verb "hebben" comes before the past participle "gehad."  
• Example 1: "Na het eten gaan we wandelen." (After eating, we go for a walk.)  
• Example 2: "Nadat hij zijn huiswerk heeft gedaan, speelt hij videogames." (After he has done his homework, he plays video games.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• De kinderen spelen in de tuin nadat ze hun huiswerk hebben gemaakt. (The children play in the garden after they have done their homework.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Bicycles are a common mode of transportation in the Netherlands. It's typical for students to ride bikes to school and park them outside during lessons.

sentences.nl: Marieke legt het plan uit, zodra iedereen buiten is.
sentences.en: Marieke explains the plan as soon as everyone is outside.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Marieke lays the plan out, as soon as everyone outside is.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The verb "legt uit" (lays out) is a separable verb. In Dutch, separable verbs often split, with the preposition moving to the end of the clause.  
• "Zodra" means "as soon as" and introduces a subordinate clause, which affects word order—placing the verb at the end.  
• Example sentences:  
  - "Hij legt het boek neer." (He puts the book down.)  
  - "Zodra het regent, ga ik naar binnen." (As soon as it rains, I go inside.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Sanne leest het verhaal voor, zodra het stil is." (Sanne reads the story aloud, as soon as it is quiet.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch culture, meetings often start with a plan or agenda. It is common to wait for everyone to be present before starting the explanation or discussion, reflecting a sense of inclusivity and order.

sentences.nl: We vertrekken naar Orvelte,, als iedereen zijn fiets heeft gecontroleerd.
sentences.en: We depart for Orvelte once everyone has checked their bike.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• We vertrekken naar Orvelte, als iedereen zijn fiets heeft gecontroleerd.  
  (We depart to Orvelte, if everyone their bike has checked.)

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses the present perfect tense ("heeft gecontroleerd") to indicate a completed action.  
• "Als" introduces a conditional clause, meaning "if" or "when," and causes inversion in the sentence structure.  
• The pronoun "zijn" is used here to indicate possession and can mean "his" or "their" (referring to "iedereen" - everyone).

- We gaan naar huis als het donker wordt. (We go home if/when it gets dark.)
- Hij belt ons als hij klaar is. (He calls us if/when he is ready.)
- Iedereen heeft zijn boek gelezen. (Everyone has read their book.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• We vertrekken naar het strand als het stopt met regenen. (We leave for the beach if it stops raining.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Orvelte is a small, picturesque village in the Netherlands known for its historical buildings and traditional Dutch countryside experience. It's a popular tourist destination for those interested in Dutch history and rural life.

sentences.nl: We rijden naar de receptie,, voordat we het vakantiepark verlaten.
sentences.en: We drive to the reception before we leave the holiday park.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• We drive to the reception, before we the holiday park leave.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• This sentence uses the present tense "rijden" (drive).  
• "Voordat" is a subordinating conjunction meaning "before," which sends the verb "verlaten" (leave) to the end of the clause.  
• Word order: In Dutch subordinate clauses, the verb typically comes at the end.  
• Additional Examples:  
  - "Ik eet ontbijt voordat ik naar school ga." (I eat breakfast before I go to school.)  
  - "Ze leest een boek voordat ze gaat slapen." (She reads a book before she goes to sleep.)  

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "We stoppen bij de supermarkt voordat we naar huis gaan." (We stop by the supermarket before we go home.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• No specific cultural note applies to this sentence.

sentences.nl: Daar haal ik wat foldertjes van Orvelte,, terwijl jullie buiten op mij wachten.
sentences.en: I'll get some leaflets from Orvelte while you wait for me outside.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• There get I some brochures from Orvelte, while you (plural) outside on me wait.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Daar haal ik wat foldertjes van Orvelte" follows the main clause structure with "daar" indicating location or point of reference, "haal ik" (I get) is the subject-verb inversion typical in Dutch main clauses.  
• "terwijl jullie buiten op mij wachten" is a subordinate clause introduced by "terwijl" (while), which places the verb at the end of the clause.  
• The diminutive "foldertjes" (brochures) uses the suffix "-tje," common in Dutch to denote smaller or more informal versions of nouns.

Examples:  
- "Daar koop ik wat brood bij de bakker." (There I buy some bread at the baker's.)  
- "Terwijl zij binnen studeert, speel ik buiten." (While she studies inside, I play outside.)  
- "We hebben wat boekjes gelezen." (We read some little books.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Daar lees ik een boek, terwijl zij een dutje doet." (There I read a book, while she takes a nap.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Orvelte is a well-preserved village in the Netherlands, known for its historical significance and traditional Dutch architecture, often attracting tourists interested in Dutch heritage.

sentences.nl: Heb ik nog tijd om een ijsje te kopen? — Nee Gianluca.
sentences.en: Do I still have time to buy an ice cream? — No Gianluca.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Have I still time to an ice cream to buy? — No Gianluca.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence is in a question format, with the verb "heb" (have) coming first, which is typical in Dutch yes/no questions.  
• "Nog" means "still," indicating continuation or remaining time.  
• The structure "om ... te + infinitive" is used for purpose or intention (to buy an ice cream).

Extra phrases:  
• Heb jij nog geld om een cadeau te kopen? (Do you still have money to buy a gift?)  
• Kan ik nog een stoel reserveren? (Can I still reserve a chair?)  
• Moet ik nog iets anders doen? (Do I still need to do anything else?)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• Mag ik nog naar het feest gaan? (May I still go to the party?)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Ice cream ("ijsje") is a popular treat in the Netherlands, especially during warmer months, and it is common to see people enjoying it in parks or while walking around cities.

sentences.nl: We wachten op elkaar, wanneer we in Orvelte aankomen.
sentences.en: We wait for each other when we arrive in Orvelte.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• We wait for each other, when we in Orvelte arrive.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• The sentence uses "wachten op" which means "to wait for." The preposition "op" is necessary in this context.  
• "Wanneer" is used as a conjunction meaning "when," introducing a subordinate clause. The verb "aankomen" (to arrive) is placed at the end of the subordinate clause, following Dutch word order rules.  
• Example 1: "Ik wacht op mijn vriend." (I am waiting for my friend.)  
• Example 2: "Wanneer hij thuiskomt, eten we." (When he comes home, we eat.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• We praten met elkaar, wanneer we thuis zijn. (We talk to each other, when we are at home.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Orvelte is a small village in the Netherlands known for its historic atmosphere and open-air museum, depicting life in the 19th century. It is a popular tourist destination.

sentences.nl: Daar maak ik 2 groepjes van vier.
sentences.en: I will make 2 groups of four from that.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• There make I 2 groups of four.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Daar" is used here to indicate "there," often used to refer back to something previously mentioned.  
• "Maak" is the verb "maken," meaning "to make" or "to create."  
• The word order is subject-verb-object; "ik" (I) is the subject, "maak" (make) is the verb, and "groepjes van vier" (groups of four) is the object.  
• "Van" is a preposition meaning "of" or "from." It's used here to indicate the composition of the groups.

Examples:  
– "Daar schrijf ik een brief." (There I write a letter.)  
– "Daar koop ik een cadeau." (There I buy a gift.)  

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Daar plan ik een feestje voor zaterdag." (There I plan a party for Saturday.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)

sentences.nl: Elke groepje krijgt een opdracht.
sentences.en: Each group receives an assignment.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Each group receives an assignment.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Elke" is a singular form meaning "each" and is used with singular nouns.  
• "Groepje" is a diminutive form of "groep" (group), indicating a small or informal group.  
• "Krijgt" is the third person singular form of the verb "krijgen" (to receive).  
• "Een opdracht" means "an assignment," where "een" is the indefinite article.

• Extra examples:  
  - "Elke student krijgt een boek." (Each student receives a book.)  
  - "Het groepje maakt een plan." (The small group makes a plan.)  
  - "Hij krijgt een cadeautje." (He receives a little gift.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Elke klas werkt aan een project." (Each class works on a project.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• [No culture note for this sentence.]

sentences.nl: Groep 1 gaat naar de klompenmakerij,, terwijl groep 2 naar de smederij gaat.
sentences.en: Group 1 goes to the clog factory, while group 2 goes to the blacksmith's shop.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Group 1 goes to the clog maker's workshop, while group 2 to the blacksmith's workshop goes.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Groep 1 gaat" and "groep 2 gaat" both use the present tense of "gaan" (to go). The structure "gaat naar" means "goes to."  
• "Terwijl" is a conjunction meaning "while" and is used to connect two clauses that happen simultaneously.  
• "De klompenmakerij" and "de smederij" are compound nouns, with "klompen" (clogs) and "smederij" (smithy/blacksmith's workshop).  
• Example phrases:  
  - "Kinderen spelen terwijl ouders praten." (Children play while parents talk.)  
  - "Hij werkt thuis, terwijl zij naar kantoor gaat." (He works at home while she goes to the office.)  
  - "Wij eten pizza terwijl we naar de film kijken." (We eat pizza while we watch the movie.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "De docent legt uit, terwijl de studenten notities maken." (The teacher explains while the students take notes.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• Klompen (wooden shoes) are a traditional Dutch footwear, often associated with rural life and Dutch heritage. Smederijen (blacksmith's workshops) were historically important in crafting tools and shoes for horses.

sentences.nl: Morgen in de les houdt elke groep een spreekbeurt.
sentences.en: Tomorrow in class, each group will give a presentation.
sentences.explanation:
## 1. Literal Translation  
• Tomorrow in the class holds every group a presentation.

## 2. Grammar Explanation and Extensions  
• "Morgen" (Tomorrow) sets the time and is placed at the beginning for emphasis.  
• "In de les" (in the class) indicates location and follows time.  
• "Houdt" (holds) is the present tense of "houden" (to hold). In Dutch, present tense can indicate future events when time is specified.  
• "Elke groep" (every group) is the subject, with "elke" meaning "every."  
• "Een spreekbeurt" (a presentation) is the direct object.

Extra examples:  
• "Volgende week gaan we naar het museum." (Next week we are going to the museum.)  
• "In de ochtend drink ik altijd koffie." (In the morning, I always drink coffee.)  
• "Elke student moet het boek lezen." (Every student must read the book.)

## 3. Create a New Example  
• "Volgende maand organiseert de club een evenement." (Next month, the club organizes an event.)

## 4. Culture Note (If there is any)  
• In Dutch schools, giving "een spreekbeurt" (a presentation) is a common part of the curriculum, often starting in primary school to help students develop public speaking skills.
